tagline: Community fork of Huly: issues, chat, CRM, HR and recruiting apps you host yourself.
description: Huly (community fork) is the Platform Collective's version of the Huly platform, a framework for business apps such as chat, project management, CRM, HRM and applicant tracking. Its README says it is a fork of Huly Platform by Hardcore Engineering Inc. and is developed independently. The original company stopped its hosted Huly service and froze its own repository, so this fork is where development continues. For issue tracking it can stand in for Linear or Asana. Production releases carry v tags and are the ones recommended for self-hosted installs; development builds use s tags and are not for production. The fork's README covers building and running the code, not a ready-made deployment guide, and it needs Docker and Docker Compose plus a recent Node.js LTS. The code is under EPL-2.0. Hardcore Engineering's separate huly-selfhost guide for the original Huly says the stack needs at least 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, with 4 vCPUs and 16 GB recommended. That figure may differ for the fork, which does not state its own.
strengths: Chat, project management, CRM, HR and recruiting apps in one codebase
Versioned production releases with v tags, kept apart from development builds
Active community development after the original company stopped its hosted service
Changelog and architecture overview kept in the repository
limits: A community fork run independently of the original company, with no hosted service behind it
No ready-made self-hosting guide in the fork's README; it documents building and running from source
Resource-heavy if it matches the original: Hardcore Engineering's guide asks for 2 vCPUs and 8 GB RAM minimum
Building needs Docker, Docker Compose and a Node.js version the README and .nvmrc state differently, so check both
Needs rush and a GitHub token to install dependencies from GitHub Packages
bestFor: A technical team that wants issues, chat and CRM in one self-run tool and can build and run from source.
